hook: Slightly charged water droplets corrode coated metal more easily
what_happened: Ni et al. showed spontaneously charged drops damage protective coatings and accelerate metal corrosion
why_it_matters: This overlooked mechanism may add to weathering of buildings, ships and cars, and points to a need for coatings that resist charge-induced damage
the_catch: The breakdown model is a lower-bound estimate assuming constant dielectric strength, though real coatings vary with thickness
caption: Charged droplets are more destructive than we thought.
alt_text: Carousel explains how slight electric charge on water drops damages coatings and speeds metal corrosion
